name: acad-files
description: AutoCAD drawing file lifecycle and conversion: open / save / save-as (with chosen DwgVersion) / close the active drawing, import DWG and DXF, export to DXF and downgraded DWG versions, plot the active layout to PDF or DWF via PlotEngine, render images, and run drawing maintenance (purge unused symbols, audit for corruption with optional fix). All operations require the AcadMcp .NET plugin loaded inside an open AutoCAD session.
intent_examples: set the drawing title and author

tools_summary.name: audit_database
tools_summary.description: Run AUDIT on the active document database. Reports the number of errors found and (if fix=true) fixed.

tools_summary.name: close_document
tools_summary.description: Close a document by its file path (or the active document if path is null). Set save=true to save before closing.

tools_summary.name: export_file
tools_summary.description: Export the active document to the given path. Format is one of "DWG", "DXF", "PDF", "DWF", "DWFX", "IMAGE" / "PNG". Optional layout name (default: current). Scope is "Display" / "Extents" / "Limits" / "Window" / "View" / "Layout". When scope="Window" you MUST supply the model-space rectangle in `window`: { xMin, yMin, xMax, yMax } in drawing units. For raster (PNG/IMAGE) and vector plots you may supply `widthPx` / `heightPx` to request an output resolution (PNG only; ignored for DWG/DXF). Typical usage for AI visual review: { format:"PNG", scope:"Window", window:{xMin:0,yMin:0,xMax:80000,yMax:60000}, widthPx:4000, heightPx:3000 }.

tools_summary.name: get_active_document
tools_summary.description: Return descriptor of the currently active document (path, name, modified flag, DWG version, entity count).

tools_summary.name: import_file
tools_summary.description: Import a .dwg / .dxf file into the currently active document at the optional insertion point (default: 0,0,0). DWG files are merged into model space; DXF respects its own units.

tools_summary.name: list_documents
tools_summary.description: List every open AutoCAD document with its file path, modified flag, read-only flag and entity count, plus the active document name.

tools_summary.name: list_drawing_properties
tools_summary.description: Read the drawing's own properties - title, subject, author, keywords, comments, last saved by, revision number, hyperlink base - plus every custom name/value pair on it. Read-only. Worth knowing: acad-fields can bind a field to any of these, so a title block that reads its project name from here updates itself instead of being retyped on every sheet.

tools_summary.name: new_document
tools_summary.description: Create a brand new empty document based on the default template (acad.dwt) and make it active.

tools_summary.name: open_document
tools_summary.description: Open an existing .dwg / .dxf file in the AutoCAD UI as a new document and make it active. Optional readOnly flag and password for encrypted DWG.

tools_summary.name: purge_database
tools_summary.description: Run a full database purge: removes every unused symbol-table record (blocks, layers, linetypes, text/dimstyle, mlinestyle, registered apps). Returns the count of records purged.

tools_summary.name: save_document
tools_summary.description: Save the currently active document to its existing path (no-op if it has no path yet — call save_document_as instead).

tools_summary.name: save_document_as
tools_summary.description: Write the active drawing to a new path. IMPORTANT: this writes a COPY. The open document keeps its own name and its own unsaved state - this is the managed Database.SaveAs, not AutoCAD's SAVEAS command, and there is no managed way to re-point an open document. So save_document afterwards still writes to the ORIGINAL path, and DBMOD still reports unsaved changes, both correctly. The result gives savedTo and the document's own path side by side, because confusing the two is the entire trap. Optional dwgVersion is one of "AC1027" (2013), "AC1032" (2018), "AC1024" (2010); defaults to native.

tools_summary.name: set_drawing_custom_property
tools_summary.description: Add, replace or remove one custom drawing property - an arbitrary name/value pair such as PROJECT-NUMBER or CLIENT. Pass value:null to remove it. These are the properties worth binding a title-block field to, because unlike the standard set they can be named after whatever the project actually tracks. The result says which of add, replace or remove happened.

tools_summary.name: set_drawing_properties
tools_summary.description: Set any of the drawing's standard properties, leaving the rest alone. Omitting a field leaves it unchanged; passing an empty string clears it deliberately - the two are different and both are supported. Custom name/value pairs go through set_drawing_custom_property instead. The result reports every property afterwards, not just the changed ones, so a caller can see that nothing else moved.
intent: set the drawing title and author
